verdict.summary: Any Help Scout user can create an OAuth app under Your Profile > My apps and any other Help Scout account can authorize it right away, with no review, marketplace or scopes. The catch is on the customer side: the Free plan has no API access, Standard can't reach reporting endpoints, and the rate limit (200–800 calls/min) is shared across the whole account.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create the app in My apps, add a redirect URL, run the authorization code flow. You need a paid plan or trial on your own account because Free has no API access.

timeToProd.assumes: A server-side agent reading and replying to conversations across customers' Help Scout accounts via the authorization code flow.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Help Scout's docs describe no review, approval or listing step for OAuth apps used by other accounts. Absence of a review step is our reading of the docs, not an explicit statement.

verdict.cost: No developer fee. Your test account and each connecting customer need a paid Help Scout plan (Standard, Plus or Pro), because the Free plan excludes API access.

Intended for internal integrations with your own account, not apps used by other Help Scout users.

steps.title: Get a paid or trial Help Scout account
steps.detail: Sign up or sign in. Make sure your plan includes API access (not Free).

steps.title: Create the OAuth app
steps.detail: Go to Your Profile > My apps > Create My App, enter a name and redirect URL, and copy the App ID and App Secret. Create it under a user who will stay on the account.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: We didn't sign in, so the exact My apps URL wasn't observed.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect users to https://secure.helpscout.net/authentication/authorizeClientApplication?client_id=...&state=.... On callback, verify state and POST grant_type=authorization_code, code, client_id, client_secret to https://api.helpscout.net/v2/oauth2/token.

steps.title: Store tokens and refresh on 401
steps.detail: Access tokens last 2 days (expires_in 172800). On HTTP 401, POST grant_type=refresh_token to the same token endpoint. Store tokens in variable-length fields and save any new refresh token returned.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Whether refresh tokens rotate on use isn't documented; saving the newest one is a precaution.

steps.title: Build plan-aware rate limiting
steps.detail: Read X-RateLimit-Limit-Minute and X-RateLimit-Remaining-Minute, count writes double, and back off on 429 using X-RateLimit-Retry-After.

steps.title: Detect plan limits per customer
steps.detail: Handle Free-plan accounts (no API) and Standard accounts (no reports) gracefully in the connect flow and feature gating.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The exact error returned to a Free-plan account wasn't documented.

steps.title: Test with a second Help Scout account
steps.detail: Authorize the app from a different account to confirm cross-account install works before launch.

blockers.symptom: A customer can authorize but API calls fail
blockers.cause: The customer is on the Free plan, which doesn't include API access.
blockers.fix: Tell the customer they need Standard, Plus or Pro before connecting.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error response for Free-plan accounts wasn't documented.

blockers.symptom: Reporting endpoints fail for some customers
blockers.cause: Standard plan accounts have no access to reporting endpoints.
blockers.fix: Hide reporting features for Standard accounts, or ask them to upgrade to Plus or Pro.

blockers.cause: The account-wide limit (200, 400 or 800 calls/min by plan) is shared by all users and integrations, and writes count double.
blockers.fix: Throttle per account, batch reads, and wait the indicated seconds.

blockers.cause: Wrong client_id or client_secret, or the app owner is no longer an active user.
blockers.fix: Check credentials, and re-create the app under an active user if the owner left.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: We observed {"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"Invalid client authentication"} with fake credentials. The link to an inactive owner is our inference from the active-user requirement.

blockers.symptom: API calls start returning 401 after about two days
blockers.fix: Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token when you get a 401.

nuances.text: OAuth credentials must belong to an active, invited user in the Help Scout account; create the app under a durable account, not a personal one that might be removed.
There are no OAuth scopes: the authorize URL takes only client_id and state, so you can't request least-privilege access, and customers can't grant partial access.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Help Scout's docs list no scope parameter; we infer the token has the full API access the plan allows.

nuances.text: Rate limits are per customer account and shared across all users and integrations, with writes counting as two requests.
Token length may change, so store access and refresh tokens in variable-length columns.
The API was renamed from Mailbox API to Inbox API; developer URLs still use /mailbox-api/.

evidence.label: tested

nuances.text: Docs API (knowledge base) is separate from the Inbox API and uses its own API key, so an agent that reads help articles needs a second credential.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Based on the Docs API being listed separately; we didn't open the Docs API auth page.
